title: Guild Decision Request
description: A decision nobody in the roster can make from the project itself, put to the human. Every request carries options, a recommendation and what happens if it goes unanswered, so a pending decision can never silently stall the work or be silently resolved by assumption. It is always answerable either as one of its listed options or as a free-text answer in the human's own words, per GUILD_MASTER_SPEC.md section 11.3 — the option set was written by a profile that could not decide, so it is never the limit of what may be answered. Red-tier actions are not decision requests: they block on an approval (guild.gate-result/v1) and never carry a default.

question.description: The decision, stated so a person can answer it without reading the repository.

raised_by.description: Canonical profile id of the profile that could not decide this inside its own boundary.

area.description: Optional. Id of the ownership area this decision belongs to.

source_question.description: Optional. Id of the ledger open question this was escalated from.

blocks.description: What is waiting on this answer: profile ids, work item ids or run ids. A decision that blocks nothing is not worth a person's attention.

option.description: Short choice key, unique within this request. Not an `id`: option keys repeat across requests by design, while every `id` in a Guild tree is globally unique.

consequence.description: What choosing this causes, in the project's own terms.

options.description: The options the asking profile could enumerate. Never the only answers available: the rendered request always also offers 'defer' and a free-text 'other'.

recommendation.description: The asking profile's own recommendation. A request with no recommendation pushes the analysis onto the human.

default_if_unanswered.description: What happens if the human does not answer. Required so work is never blocked indefinitely — and so a default is never applied without the human having been shown it first.

in_force_from.description: When the default takes effect: a date, or the event that triggers it.

revisit_when.description: What brings this back to the human. A default is provisional, never a closed decision.

status.description: open: raised, not yet put to the human. presented: the human has seen it in the canonical format. answered: the human chose. deferred: the human explicitly chose to decide later, and the default is in force. withdrawn: no longer needed.

answered_by.description: 'human', or the canonical profile id the human delegated it to.

answer.description: The chosen option key, or the human's own answer verbatim when it is none of the options. A free-text answer is recorded exactly as given rather than mapped onto the nearest option.

answer_kind.description: How the human answered: by choosing a listed option, in their own words, or by explicitly deferring. Required once status is 'answered' or 'deferred' — it is what distinguishes an answer that fits the options from one that did not, and keeps a free-text answer from being quietly recorded as an option key.

resulting_decision.description: Optional. Id of the decision record this answer produced.
